easy.def: To throw or move things all over.
examples: We scatter seeds for the birds.
The wind scatters the leaves.
The birds scattered when the cat came.

more.def: To throw or spread things over a wide area, or to move apart quickly.
examples: The marbles scattered across the floor when the bag broke.
The crowd scattered when the rain began.
He scattered salt on the icy steps.

easy.def: One of the four parts of the year.
examples: Winter is the cold season.
What season is your birthday in?
Summer is the hot season.

more.def: One of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, fall, and winter.
examples: Fall is my favorite season because the leaves change color.
Soccer season starts in the spring.
Strawberries are in season in early summer.

easy.def: Something you do not tell other people.
examples: The gift is a secret.
Can you keep a secret?
I have a secret hiding spot.

more.def: Something that is kept hidden or known by only a few people.
examples: She kept the surprise party a secret for two weeks.
The recipe is a family secret.
He whispered the secret to his best friend.
It is selfish not to share.
The selfish cat took the whole bed.
Do not be selfish with the ball.

more.def: Caring only about yourself and not about other people.
examples: It was selfish of him to eat the whole cake without sharing.
A selfish player never passes the ball.
She realized it was selfish to keep the window seat every time.

easy.def: A dark shape made when something blocks the light.
examples: I can see my shadow on the wall.
My shadow is long in the evening.
The cat jumped at its own shadow.

more.def: A dark shape that forms when something blocks light.
examples: In the evening, the trees cast long shadows across the lawn.
The tall building cast a shadow over the park.
We made shadow animals on the wall with our hands.
We found shelter from the rain.
The cat found shelter under the porch.
The bus stop is a shelter from the wind.

more.def: A place that covers and protects people or animals from weather or danger.
examples: The hikers built a shelter out of branches before the storm.
The barn gave the cows shelter from the snow.
People who lost their homes stayed at a shelter.

easy.def: To shake because you are cold or scared.
examples: I shiver in the snow.
The wet dog shivers.
The scary story made me shiver.

more.def: To shake slightly because you are cold or frightened.
examples: We shivered at the bus stop in the icy wind.
The swimmers shivered as they climbed out of the lake.
He shivered when the cold wind blew down his neck.
The house was silent at night.
The class was silent for the test.
Snow makes the world silent.
The forest was silent after the snowfall.
The crowd fell silent when the music began.
She stayed silent because she did not know the answer.
Our shoes are similar. They are both blue.
The two cats look similar.
A lemon is similar to a lime.

more.def: Alike in many ways, but not exactly the same.
examples: A wolf looks similar to a large dog.
Their voices are so similar that I mix them up on the phone.
The two towns have similar weather.
This puzzle is simple.
The game has simple rules.
I made a simple lunch.

more.def: Easy to understand or do; not hard or complicated.
examples: The directions were simple, so we finished quickly.
She wore a simple blue dress.
There is a simple way to fix the problem.

easy.def: All the bones in a body.
examples: Your skeleton holds you up.
A fish has a skeleton too.
We saw a skeleton in science class.

more.def: The frame of bones that supports the body of a person or animal.
examples: The museum has the skeleton of a huge dinosaur.
The human skeleton has more than two hundred bones.
We found the skeleton of a small bird in the woods.

easy.def: So wet or smooth that you might slide.
examples: The ice is slippery.
The wet floor is slippery.
A fish is slippery to hold.

more.def: So smooth, wet, or icy that it is hard to hold or walk on.
examples: Be careful, because the floor is slippery when it is wet.
The soap was too slippery to hold.
Wet leaves made the sidewalk slippery.

easy.def: A way to fix a problem.
examples: I found a solution. We can share the toy!
What is the solution to the math problem?
The solution was to ask for help.

more.def: The answer to a problem or the way to fix it.
examples: The solution to the puzzle was hidden in the last clue.
There is no easy solution to the traffic problem.
The class worked together to find a solution.
Hold the ladder steady.
The boat is steady on the calm lake.
Use a steady hand to pour the milk.

more.def: Firm and not shaking; also, not changing much.
examples: She kept a steady hand while she painted the tiny flowers.
A steady rain fell all day.
He walked at a steady pace for miles.
I heard a strange noise.
What a strange hat!
The food had a strange smell.

more.def: Unusual, odd, or not known to you.
examples: A strange light was blinking in the sky.
It felt strange to be at school at night.
The scientist found a strange new insect.

easy.def: Not wanting to change your mind.
examples: The stubborn puppy would not come inside.
My stubborn dog will not take a bath.
Do not be stubborn. Try the peas.

more.def: Refusing to change your mind or do what others want.
examples: He was too stubborn to admit that he was lost.
The stubborn stain would not come out.
The stubborn mule refused to cross the bridge.

easy.def: Something you did not know would happen.
examples: The party was a surprise!
I have a surprise for you!
What a nice surprise to see you!

more.def: Something that happens that you did not expect.
examples: It was a nice surprise to find a letter in the mailbox.
To my surprise, the cat liked the bath.
The ending of the book was a complete surprise.
Plants need water to survive.
Fish can not survive out of water.
The plant survived the cold.

more.def: To stay alive, especially through something hard or dangerous.
examples: Camels can survive for days without drinking water.
The sailors survived the storm.
Few plants can survive in such dry soil.
